name: Beth Hansen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does your day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43, have a bachelor's degree, and became the junior manager of branch leases at a large company last winter. I lead three officers and keep twelve rent deadlines straight, though my senior officer still catches adjustments I miss. I like visiting a branch before a move and hearing what staff need; I hate a tidy lease file that leaves someone locked out on opening day.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How are things outside that office?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner runs a mechanic shop with regular work, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My salary is high for this job and we have around eleven months of expenses saved, with plenty of similar employers nearby. I don't use AI tools; I prefer a wall sheet and a signed copy I can point to.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say an automatic reminder for a lease renewal is harmless, but I still need to read the signed rent schedule before a branch moves. Our staff live with the dates on a signed rent schedule, not with a reminder.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I joined the lease team as its junior manager last winter and still need my senior officer to check the rent adjustments. My partner's mechanic shop has regular work, my manager pay is high, and we have eleven months of expenses saved; with two children and a mortgage, that security is a relief, not an invitation to gamble.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll keep the paper tickler file for every branch lease and have the senior officer sign off the annual rent list. In the first year of a plateau, we'll continue the 250 monthly extra mortgage payment while the shop income holds and I will ask for one more walk-through before any branch handover.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about our income. I am more bothered by an avoidable move that gives a worker a longer school journey than by a small reminder program.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which date nearly slipped recently?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A landlord sent a notice to the wrong branch inbox, and the renewal deadline was two weeks away when my officer found it. I went to the branch and confirmed the manager had the correct signed copy before we answered the landlord.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep paper when the company has a digital file?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can see all twelve deadlines on one wall sheet and put a finger on the next one. I don't use AI tools, and I won't swap a routine I can check for a screen I don't yet trust.

say: I'd accept **lease reminders** while keeping a human check on signed rent schedules.
I'd tell colleagues a branch move affects **school journeys**, not just calendar dates.
think: Our **eleven-month reserve** and the mechanic shop's regular work keep money secure in a plateau.
As a junior manager, I still need **senior checks** on rent adjustments.
do: Keep the **wall deadline sheet** and get senior sign-off on rent lists.
Pay an **extra 250 monthly** toward the mortgage while shop income holds.
feel: She feels **calm** about income and attentive to the families affected by branch moves.
S0.quote: Our staff live with the dates on a signed rent schedule, not with a reminder.
fieldNote: Her **strong reserve** and high pay make small automation feel manageable, even with children and a mortgage.
She trusts the **twelve-date wall sheet** after a notice reached the wrong inbox.

steps.text: Keep twelve branch lease deadlines on the wall sheet this month
Pay an extra 250 monthly toward mortgage while shop income holds

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our lease office Steady Disruption will take the first pass at contracts, booking moves and answering landlord questions. I would ask for a trial that includes the awkward cases where a branch cannot move during school exams.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own work is reading and scheduling, and a regional manager could probably absorb it if the software works. We have savings and other local employers, but I am still learning the role; I would not assume my desk survives because I know the landlords' names.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll bring six difficult branch moves to the director and ask for a written staffing plan before any new system is bought. In the first year of disruption, if the lease office is merged, I'd check property coordinator openings at three nearby employers and accept a role only after comparing the pay and school pickup hours with my partner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the desk being folded away, even with a full savings account. My family can absorb a search, but I don't enjoy spending our children's security to prove I can change jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you test the software yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd let the senior officer and our technology team run it on copies and show me which dates it misses. I would read the results, but I won't claim I use AI; I have never used those tools myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a property coordinator job acceptable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The wage must keep the mortgage current without raiding savings every month, and I need to be home for the younger child's pickup when my partner closes the shop. A property vacancy notice won't tell me whether the wage covers our mortgage or the hours fit school pickup.

say: I'd demand a **difficult-case trial** covering moves during school exams.
I'd ask for a **staffing plan** before the company buys a lease system.
think: A regional manager could absorb my **reading and scheduling** if software handles the first pass.
Savings and local employers help, but my **junior post** is not guaranteed.
do: Bring **six hard moves** to the director and seek staffing terms this month.
If merged, check **property vacancies** at three nearby employers.
Accept only **mortgage-covering pay** without monthly reserve use and hours allowing our younger child's pickup.
feel: She feels **anxious** about her own desk disappearing, despite a long reserve.
S1.quote: A property vacancy notice won't tell me whether the wage covers our mortgage or the hours fit school pickup.
fieldNote: She will **read trial results** but leaves AI testing to colleagues, matching her resistance to personal use.
Her job search is bounded by **mortgage pay** and a child's school pickup, not only geography.

steps.text: Check property coordinator openings at three nearby employers if lease office merges

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AGI by 2028 could read leases and plan moves at a cost our office cannot match, and people need notice before the company closes the desk. I would ask who answers for a wrong rent date that forces a branch into a bad lease.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This job is mostly thinking work, so AGI reaches me in 2028; robots around 2031 are for physical moves and give my desk no extra time. I expect my post could be cut, but eleven months saved and my partner's shop income mean we can search without missing the next mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll gather copies of the twelve branch leases and ask for the decision date on our posts. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if I am cut, I'd apply to local property offices with posted wages that cover the mortgage and pickup schedule, and accept only a written offer; if the search lasts six months, we'd ask my partner's shop accountant whether extra owner drawings are safe rather than assume they are.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, not helpless. We have time to look, but I would hate to explain to our children why a branch decision put our own home into question.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move your family for a new job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not in the first year; there are enough employers within a drive that I would search locally first. A move would disturb both children's schools and my partner's shop, and I would not make that choice on a speculative opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the branch staff?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell them the company is reviewing leases and that I can't promise their location will stay. I would not show branch staff a machine-generated move date until someone had checked the signed lease.

say: I'd seek **notice** and accountability for wrong rent dates before the 2028 change.
I'd tell staff **lease reading** changes with AGI, before physical moving robots arrive.
think: AGI reaches my **desk in 2028**; robots around 2031 do not delay the exposure.
Eleven months saved and shop income protect the next payment, though my **post may go**.
do: Gather **twelve signed leases** and ask for a staffing decision date now.
After 2028, seek **local property work** with posted mortgage-covering pay and pickup hours; accept only a written offer.
After six months searching, ask the **shop accountant** whether extra owner drawings are safe.
feel: She feels **anxious** about losing her post, while able to search without an immediate missed mortgage.
S2.quote: I would not show branch staff a machine-generated move date until someone had checked the signed lease.
fieldNote: She names the **2028 desk shock** while treating 2031 moving robots as a separate later change.
Her reserve buys **search time**; family schools and the shop keep her from planning a speculative move.

steps.text: Apply to local property offices after 2028 if posted pay covers mortgage and school pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our lease team AGI by 2031 gives us five years to find different duties within the company, but the company must name real posts. I would ask the branch managers what went wrong on past moves before we write any new process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: More time lets me move toward branch handovers, where visiting a site and speaking with staff are part of the day. AGI still reaches contract reading and move planning in 2031, and even handover decisions could be automated; robots around 2034 might later handle physical moving, so this isn't a safe hiding place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting next spring, I'd use up to 900 from our separate training budget for a building-access course and personally inspect three branch handovers with the site manager. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd seek a branch handover post only if one is open with pay that covers the mortgage; otherwise I'd check local property firms while keeping my current wage until I have an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy, and I like having five years to practise on actual sites. I am not eager to become the person who signs off a machine's move plan without seeing the doorway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you inspect at a handover?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd check whether keys, lifts and access for a wheelchair work on the day staff arrive. A spotless lease file won't help someone who cannot get through the door.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course costs more than 900?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd find a cheaper one or skip it; the 900 is what my partner and I set aside for training. We won't turn our emergency fund into a blank cheque for a certificate.

say: I'd ask for **real posts** and lessons from past branch moves before 2031.
I'd tell staff **site handovers** need inspection, even as contract work changes.
think: Five years lets me practise **site handovers**, though AGI may automate their planning too.
Robots around **2034** might reach physical moves, so handover work is not permanent shelter.
do: Spend at most **900** from training cash on building access and inspect three handovers next spring.
After 2031, seek a **handover vacancy** only with mortgage-covering pay; otherwise search local firms while employed.
feel: She feels **uneasy**, with time to inspect real sites before choosing another post.
S3.quote: A spotless lease file won't help someone who cannot get through the door.
fieldNote: Her planned move uses **self-funded site learning**, avoiding a speculative promise of employer-paid training.
She explicitly sees **handover planning** as thinking-exposed and keeps pay and vacancy conditions.

steps.text: Take building-access course costing at most 900 from separate training budget
Inspect three branch handovers with the site manager next spring
Apply for branch handover only if vacancy pays mortgage after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the branch team AGI by 2036 is a decade away, and we should write down the human costs of each move while we still make decisions. I would ask for an annual record of actual branch moves, not a list of promised efficiencies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I might have less mortgage and children through school, and our savings let me choose carefully. Yet lease reading and handover planning are thinking work that AGI could do in 2036; robots around 2039 are later and would only touch the physical moving side.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep reviewing the signed lease dates and volunteer for one branch walk-through each quarter if the site manager can take me. In the first year after 2036, I'd keep a branch services role only if a person still owns the move decision at viable pay; otherwise I'd apply to other local employers without resigning until a written offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel watchful rather than frightened. Ten years lets me test whether I really like site work before giving up a well-paid desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay down the mortgage faster during the decade?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We'd continue the 250 extra monthly payment as long as the shop's work remains steady. I would not empty the emergency account to make the mortgage statement look nicer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a move decision worth owning?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A branch manager could call me when a child-care problem makes a planned relocation impossible, and I could change the date. If my name is only on an automatic notice, I haven't made a decision at all.

say: I'd ask for **annual move records** that show staff consequences, not promised efficiencies.
I'd tell branches a **decade** is time to check real handovers before 2036.
think: At **53**, mortgage and school duties may ease, but desk planning still faces 2036 AGI.
Robots around **2039** touch physical moves later, not my lease decisions.
do: Keep **signed lease checks** and join quarterly branch walk-throughs if a site manager can host me.
After 2036, keep **viable decision work** or seek local offers while remaining employed.
feel: She feels **watchful** with ten years to try site work without risking the family reserve.
S4.quote: If my name is only on an automatic notice, I haven't made a decision at all.
fieldNote: Her long-run test is **actual authority** to change a move date when staff lives require it.
She retains **written-offer and pay conditions**, and keeps emergency cash separate from extra mortgage payments.

steps.text: Keep checking signed branch lease dates this year
Join quarterly branch walk-throughs if site manager can host
Seek local work after 2036 if viable decision work ends; keep wage until signed offer

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because reading and planning the branch moves could be cheaper before I have enough experience at handovers. A real staffing date, permission to visit sites, and a written offer with mortgage-covering pay would help me decide without gambling our savings.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the branch worker who has to change a child's school route when a move date shifts. The rent schedule is not the only calendar in a relocation.

headlineQuote: The rent schedule is not the only calendar in a relocation.
portrait: At **43**, Beth is a junior branch lease manager who still needs a senior officer's check on rent adjustments.
Her **eleven-month reserve**, high pay and the family mechanic shop give choices, while school pickup and mortgage terms still matter.
She avoids **AI tools** and tests a possible move by walking sites and checking signed leases.
Fast AGI threatens **lease planning**; longer runways let her learn handovers, which may also be automated.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her lease role before she gains enough site handover experience.
whatWouldHelp: A **staffing date**, site access and a written mortgage-covering offer would let her choose carefully.
